deep.reconstruction:
OVERVIEW. Most of the page derives a product (transformation) formula for p-th order Riemann theta functions in g variables. Riemann's convention is ϑ(a;w)=Σ_{n∈Z^g} exp(Σ a_{νν'} n_ν n_ν' + 2Σ n_ν w_ν). A notation such as ϑ(c(a;w)) means the series with the whole exponent multiplied by c. A separate block at the bottom evaluates a finite alternating binomial sum, which is a Stirling-number identity.

(1) Trial substitutions (top left). The fragments 'p-1 u+u=u′, v−v=v′', 'p-1 v+αu, v+βu', '(p-1)^2 v_ν+(p-1)u_ν', '(p-2)p v_ν+p u_ν' are searches for a linear change of summation indices. The aim is to split a product of two theta series into a sum of other theta products. The exponent fragments e^{(p-1)(Σa n n+2Σu n)}… are trials of the same kind.

(2) The product to be transformed (top right). This is Σ_n e^{p/(p-1)(Σa_{νν'}n_νn_ν'+2Σn_νv_ν)} · Σ_m e^{p(Σa_{νν'}m_νm_ν'+2Σm_νu_ν)} = ϑ(p/(p-1)(a;v)) ϑ(p(a;u)).

(3) Key substitution. Riemann sets v′=(p−1)u−v and u′=u+v. Inverting gives pu=u′+v′ and pv=(p−1)u′−v′.
- [mine] The quadratic identity behind this is (1/(p−1))((p−1)x−y)^2+(x+y)^2 = p x^2 + p/(p−1) y^2. It holds equally for the bilinear form Σa_{νν'}.
- [mine] Put n′=(p−1)m−n and m′=m+n. Then p/(p−1)Q(n)+pQ(m)+2p/(p−1) n·v+2p m·u = (1/(p−1))(Q(n′)+2n′·v′)+Q(m′)+2m′·u′.
- [mine] The pairs (n′,m′) that occur are exactly those with n′+m′=pm≡0 (mod p), a sublattice of index p^g.
- This yields Riemann's line ϑ(1/(p−1)(a;(p−1)u−v)) ϑ(a;u+v) = f(v,u). Summed over all (n′,m′), this product contains the original product as a sub-sum.

(4) Quasi-periodicity of f.
- Riemann checks how log f changes under u_ν′ → u_ν′ + a_{νν′}.
  - The first factor contributes (p−1)a_{ν′ν′}+2((p−1)u−v)_{ν′}. This is obtained by applying the period shift p−1 times to the 1/(p−1)-series [mine].
  - The second factor contributes a_{ν′ν′}+2(u+v)_{ν′}.
  - Total: log f(v,u) = p a_{ν′ν′}+2p u_{ν′} + log f(v,u+a_{·ν′}).
- Similarly, for v → v + a_{·ν′} the pieces (1/(p−1))(2(v−(p−1)u)+a)+a+2(v+u) sum to log f(v,u) = p/(p−1)(a_{ν′ν′}+2v_{ν′}) + log f(v+a,u).
- These are exactly the quasi-periodicity factors of ϑ(p/(p−1)(a;v))·ϑ(p(a;u)).
- f is also invariant under shifts of v by (p−1)πi/p·ε and of u by πi/p·ε. These are periodic in ε with period p ('f(ε+p)=f(ε)').
- This is the Riemann–Hermite method: identify a theta product by its quasi-periodicity together with a finite character decomposition.

(5) Character (Fourier) decomposition. Riemann inserts Σ_ε α^{Σε_νλ_ν}, with α a primitive p-th root of unity and ε_ν=0..p−1, to cut out the residue classes of the summation lattice. The condition 'p n_ν ≡ −λ_ν' marks the residue class. The final formula reads:

A·ϑ(1/(p−1)(pa;(p−1)u′−v′)) ϑ(pa;u′+v′) = Σ_ε α^{Σε_νλ_ν} ϑ(1/(p−1)(a; v′−ε_ν(p−1)πi/p)) ϑ(a; u′+ε_νπi/p).

The left side is just the original product rewritten, since (p−1)u′−v′=pv and u′+v′=pu. For λ=0 one gets A=p^g [mine]. Riemann writes the ε-sum as (Σ_0^{p−1})^p, so here the number of variables is also called p. For λ≠0 the left side becomes a theta product with characteristics λ/p. For g=1 this is Schröter's formula with weights (1,p−1). For p=2 it is the classical second-order addition formula ϑ(2a;2u)ϑ(2a;2v) ↔ Σ_ε ϑ(a;u+v+·)ϑ(a;u−v+·).

(6) Bottom block: an alternating sum. Riemann evaluates S = Σ_{k≥0} (−1)^k C(p−1,k)(p−1−k)^p, the same sum as d^p/dv^p (e^v−1)^{p−1} at v=0, i.e. (x∂_x)^p (x−1)^{p−1} at x=1.
- With x=1+y he applies D=(1+y)∂_y to y^{p−1} p times. He tracks only the two lowest terms a_ν y^{p−ν−1}+b_ν y^{p−ν}.
- Since D y^k = k y^{k−1}+k y^k, the recursion is a_{ν+1}=(p−ν−1)a_ν and b_{ν+1}=(p−ν)b_ν+a_{ν+1}, with a_0=1, b_0=0.
- Hence a_ν=Π(p−1)/Π(p−ν−1), i.e. Π(p−ν−1)a_ν=α:=Π(p−1).
- Put β_ν=Π(p−ν)b_ν. Then β_{ν+1}=β_ν+(p−ν−1)α with β_0=0. So β_ν=(νp−ν(ν+1)/2)α.
- The value at y=0 after p steps is b_p=β_p/Π(0)=p(p−1)/2·Π(p−1).
- So S=(p−1)!·C(p,2)=(p−1)!·S(p,p−1), where S(p,p−1) is a Stirling number of the second kind.
- The purpose is probably a normalising or counting constant in the theta computation, but the page does not say.
errors: The written relation f(v_ν+ε_ν(p−1)πi/p, u_ν) = f(v_ν, u_ν+ε_νπi/p) has a sign slip. The left side multiplies the terms by α^{−ε(n′+m′)}, so it equals f(v, u−επi/p). This is harmless when summing over all ε.

In the final formula the shifts v′−ε(p−1)πi/p and u′+επi/p produce the character α^{ε(m′−n′)}. The lattice condition, however, is n′+m′≡0 (mod p), which needs both shifts with the same sign (or f(v+ε(p−1)πi/p,u)). This is consistent with the previous slip and does not affect the structure.
The constant A is left undetermined; for λ=0 it should be p^g (p^p in Riemann's indexing).
The fragment 'a_{ν,ν′}+2u_{ν′}+v_{ν′}' should read a_{ν′ν′}+2(u_{ν′}+v_{ν′}); possibly a transcription issue.
The bookkeeping uses p both for the transformation order and for the number of variables (ε_1…ε_p). This is ambiguous but not a mathematical error.

results.what: Product formula: ϑ(p/(p−1)(a;v))·ϑ(p(a;u)) expressed as a character-weighted sum over ε∈(Z/p)^g of ϑ(1/(p−1)(a;(p−1)u−v+shift))·ϑ(a;u+v+shift), via the lattice substitution n′=(p−1)m−n, m′=m+n
results.modern_name: Multi-variable Schröter formula (special case (1,p−1)); a Koizumi-type theta product formula; for p=2 the Riemann/Jacobi second-order addition formula
results.usually_credited_to: Schröter 1854 (g=1); multivariable versions Hermite, Königsberger, Prym–Krazer (1860s–1890s); general form Koizumi 1976

results.what: Quasi-periodicity check of f(v,u) under shifts by periods a_{·ν′}, showing it matches that of the product theta (Riemann–Hermite characterisation method)
results.modern_name: Automorphy factors of theta functions; characterisation of theta functions of order n

results.what: Σ_k (−1)^k C(p−1,k)(p−1−k)^p = (p−1)!·p(p−1)/2, via a recursion for ((1+y)∂_y)^p y^{p−1}
results.modern_name: Finite-difference formula for Stirling numbers of the second kind: S(p,p−1)=C(p,2)

deep.surprise_reason: The derivation is a correct multi-variable Schröter-type theta product formula, obtained by Riemann's quasi-periodicity and character method. Such formulas were standard material in theta transformation theory by the 1860s (Schröter 1854 for one variable, later Königsberger and Prym–Krazer). The adjacent pages (quartic surfaces with 16 nodes, i.e. Kummer surfaces) suggest a date around 1864 rather than 1853. It is a nice unpublished detail of Riemann working with general-genus theta products, but not a result credited to anyone much later. The Stirling sum is routine.

transcription_corrections: Top-right second factor: 'Σ e^{p(Σ a_{ν,ν′} + 2Σ n_ν u_ν)}' should be Σ e^{p(Σ a_{ν,ν′} n_ν n_ν′ + 2Σ n_ν u_ν)}.
'(p−1)u_ν − v_ν = v′_ν': the operator sign is over-written in the image, but the later lines p u=u′+v′ and p v=(p−1)u′−v′ force the minus sign.
'a_{ν,ν′} + 2u_{ν′} + v_{ν′}' is the second piece of the automorphy factor and should read a_{ν′ν′} + 2(u_{ν′}+v_{ν′}).
In 'log f(v_ν; u_ν) = ?/(p−1)(v_ν − p−1 u_ν) + …' the coefficient is 2/(p−1) together with an a_{ν′ν′}/(p−1) term, i.e. (1/(p−1))(2(v−(p−1)u)+a).
'pν ≡ λ_ν' and 'p a_ν ≡ [?]' are most likely congruences on summation indices (p m_ν ≡ λ_ν, p n_ν ≡ −λ_ν).
Bottom right 'a_0 = Π(p−1) a_ν [?]' is most likely α = Π(p−ν−1)a_ν (with a_0=1, α=Π(p−1)), as in the middle line 'Π(p−ν−1)a_ν = α'.
'β_ν = Π(p−ν−1) b_{ν+1} = Π(p−ν)b_ν + a_{ν+1}Π(p−ν−1)' should be read as β_{ν+1} = Π(p−ν−1) b_{ν+1} = Π(p−ν) b_ν + Π(p−ν−1) a_{ν+1}.

'∂_y^{p−ν}(a_ν y^{p−ν−1} + b_ν y^{p−ν})' denotes the state after ν applications of (1+y)∂_y (lowest two terms), not a pure ∂_y derivative; the next term should read (1+y)((p−ν−1)a_ν y^{p−ν−2} + b_ν(p−ν) y^{p−ν−1}).
